summary: The patch silences the warning by calling self._check_feature_names(X, reset=True) on the internally-validated ndarray, which has the side effect of deleting the fitted feature_names_in_ attribute. This trades the spurious warning for a real regression in fitted-estimator state.

issues.description: By the offset_ computation step X is the validated ndarray (no feature names). _check_feature_names(X, reset=True) on an input without feature names does not just 'validate' — it delattr's feature_names_in_. The warning disappears only because the attribute is destroyed, so the subsequent reset=False check inside score_samples finds nothing to compare. This is a hacky fix exploiting a destructive side effect rather than suppressing the warning correctly (e.g. a private _score_samples that skips re-validation, or warnings.catch_warnings).

Concrete regression: after fitting IsolationForest on a DataFrame with contamination != 'auto', clf.feature_names_in_ is deleted and no longer exists, violating the estimator contract. Existing common tests (check_dataframe_column_names_consistency) use default contamination='auto', which hits the early-return branch before this line, so they never exercise the path — that's why the suite still passes despite the broken behavior.
Comment 'Validate feature names before calling score_samples' mischaracterizes the call — its actual operative effect here is resetting/removing feature_names_in_, not validation.
